1.w: After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed his day.

3.w: “May the day perish on which I was born, and the night [that] one said, ‘A male child has been conceived.’

4.w: That day—may it be darkness; let not God seek it above, nor let light shine upon it.

5.w: Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it; may a cloud dwell over it; let the blackness of the day terrify it.

6.w: That night—let darkness take it! Let it not it rejoice among the days of the year; into the number of the months let it not come.

7.w: Behold, that night—may it be barren, let no joyful shout come into it.

8.w: May they curse it, those cursing the day, those ready to rouse Leviathan.

9.w: May the stars of its morning light be dark; may it look for light and there [be] none, and do not let it see the eyelids of the dawn;

10.w: for it did not shut the doors of my womb, and hide trouble from my eyes.

11.w: Why did I not die from the womb? I should have come forth from the belly and expired!

12.w: Why did the knees meet me, and why the breasts that I should suck?

13.w: For now I would have lain down and been quiet; I would have slept—then there would be rest for me

14.w: with the kings and counselors of the earth, who built [up] ruins for themselves;

15.w: or with the princes [with] gold unto them, those filling their houses [with] silver.

16.w: Or [why] was I not hidden like a stillborn child, like infants [who] had not seen the light?

17.w: There the wicked cease [from] trouble, and there those weary of power are at rest—

18.w: together the captives are at rest; they do not hear the voice oppressing [them].

19.w: The small and the great there the same, and the servant [is] free from his master.

20.w: Why is light given to the one toiling, and life to the bitter of soul,

21.w: those waiting for death and there is none, and those digging for it more than hidden treasures,

22.w: those being glad unto joy; they rejoice that they should find the grave?

23.w: To a man [for] whom his path is hidden, and God has hedged around him?

24.w: For before my food my sighing comes, and my groanings pour out like the waters.

25.w: For the dreadful thing I dreaded, and it has met me, and that which I had feared has come to me.

26.w: I am not at ease, nor am I quiet; and I do not have rest, and turmoil has come.”
